title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-19
korean_summary: 내일 핵심(목): 본사 10월 실적·11~2월 예상손익 11/20(금) 기한 → 오늘 법인장 초안 보고, 회계 11월 세무단가 재승인 요청(이상 수치 확인 후 승인), 수출입 신고 누락 전수 확인 오늘 기한. 손익 차이 파일·퇴사 처리·소방 재견적도 오늘.
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Thursday, November nineteenth. This is your English briefing for today.

Yesterday was a busy and good day. You sent the answer about work accident costs to the head office. You reported the tax office case to my director. You sent the weekly headcount, and my director said okay. You also sent the October financial statements to the head office. So today we start with a cleaner desk.

We have eight parts today. Part one is a short opening, and you are hearing it now. Part two is the top three for today. Part three is reports to collect. Part four is replies you owe. Part five is the schedule and deadlines. Part six is an English review. Part seven is a short role-play. Part eight is the closing. Let's start.
Part two. The top three for today.
Number one. The forecast for the head office.

What is it? Yesterday afternoon, a head office manager sent a notice about the monthly profit and loss report. She wants two things. First, the October actual results. Second, the forecast from November to February next year. The head office checked that every factory will have at least a minimum share of its lines filled until February. So she wants the forecast made on that basis. The deadline is tomorrow, Friday, November twentieth.

Why is it important? Last week the forecast was for November to January. Now it goes one month longer, to February. My director must review it before it goes out. And your calendar also shows the profit report on Friday.

Your first action today. Add the February column to the forecast file this morning. Use the minimum line rule for every month. Then show a first draft to my director after lunch, so he has time to check it.
Number two. The chief accountant's new tax price plan.

What is it? At four thirty yesterday afternoon, the chief accountant wrote to you. She asked you to approve the tax price plan for November again. The reason is that the shipping plan changed on November fourteenth. Now the quantity for November is much bigger, and the gap between the price and the tax price is bigger too.

Why is it important? This number goes straight into the profit forecast. So item one and item two are connected. Also, one figure in her mail looks wrong. For the main buyer, the tax price is higher than the real price. That does not match the total. Please check it before you approve.

Your first action today. Open her file and compare it with the shipping plan of November fourteenth. Ask her about the strange figure. Approve only after the numbers match. Then use the new numbers in the forecast.
Number three. The full check of declarations by the export staff.

What is it? This is about the tax office case. Some sample shipments were declared under our tax code by another office, and we were not aware of them. The export staff promised to check all declarations by today, November nineteenth. Yesterday, a head office manager in the head office also replied with the cause and the list of people who booked each shipment. You sent him the list of samples you know about since April, and asked for his opinion on how to handle them.
Why is it important? My director thanked you yesterday for moving this forward. But if there are more missing cases, the tax office can find them later. It is better that we find them first.
Your first action today. Ask the export staff for her full check result by noon. Compare it with a head office manager's list. If there are new cases, report them to my director in one short mail.
Part three. Reports to collect.

First, the cost accountant. Her Manage versus Tax file for October is due today. This file shows the difference between the management profit and the tax profit. When you check it, look at the October column only, and make sure the total matches the profit and loss file. Here is a sentence you can use. "Hi, could you send me the October column of the Manage versus Tax file by 3 PM today?"

Second, the HR staff. The resignation of one worker should be finished today. This is on your instruction list. Check that the final pay date and the papers are ready. Also, yesterday the HR staff told you that some short-term workers in the warehouse will finish on November nineteenth and twenty-fifth. Here is a sentence. "Hi, please confirm that the resignation papers are done, and tell me if anything is still open."

Third, the compliance officer. She owes you a new quotation for the fire system maintenance today. Yesterday she also sent one more quotation for the electrical inspection,. Now you have more suppliers for the electrical inspection. Here is a sentence. "Hi, thank you for the third quote. Please send me the new fire system quote today, on the same conditions as the others."

Fourth, the IT staff. Yesterday you asked him to get quotes for the cutting machine parts in the pattern room. The machine works now, so you want to compare prices before the purchase request. A purchase request is the form we use to buy things. Here is a sentence. "Hi, please get at least two quotes for the cable and the cushion, so that we can compare prices before the purchase request."

Fifth, the purchasing staff. Yesterday afternoon you asked her for quotations to replace the boiler feed water pumps. This will take some days, but ask for a date. "Hi, when can you send me the pump quotations? Please give me a date."

Sixth, the warehouse leader. She sent you the email address of the new statistic staff yesterday. Her training checklist and schedule are due tomorrow, Friday. "Hi, please send me the training checklist and the schedule by tomorrow noon."
Part four. Replies I owe.

First, the chief accountant. This is the tax price plan from part two. She is waiting for your approval. Your first sentence can be: "Hi, thank you for the update. Before I approve, I would like to check one figure."

Second, the accountant. Yesterday you sent her a revised file for the insurance renewal. She has not replied yet. If she replies today, check that the broker received the new file. Your first sentence can be: "Hi, did the broker confirm the revised file? Please let me know by today."

Third, a head office manager, about the labor contracts for January. Yesterday you asked her to review one sewing operator again. The worker is pregnant, and this was not shown in the first file. Wait for her answer. If she replies, tell the HR staff right away. Your first sentence to the HR staff can be: "Hi, the head office has replied about the pregnant worker. Please prepare the contract as below."

Fourth, a head office manager. You asked him for his opinion on future sample shipments. If he answers, thank him and agree on one simple rule. For example, every sample under our name must be reported to our factory on the same day. Your first sentence can be: "Thank you for your advice. My understanding is that the sales team will tell us before each shipment. Please correct me if I'm wrong."
Part five. The schedule and deadlines.

Today, Thursday. You have the overtime plan for next week on your calendar. The declaration check from the export team, the Manage versus Tax file, the worker resignation, and the fire system quotation are all due today.

Tomorrow, Friday, November twentieth. At twelve noon, the head office organization chart and headcount update. Also on Friday: the profit report and forecast to a head office manager, the weekly cash flow, the weekly outsourcing report, the export and import cost ledger check, and the warehouse leader's training checklist.
Saturday, November twenty-first. The sales team debit closing is on your calendar. Also, the labor contract for the pregnant sewing operators is due.
Part six. English review.
Let's review seven expressions from this week.

The expression is: cross-check. It means to check one record against another record. For example, who cross-checks the trucking invoice against the booking? Now say it with me.
... ... ...
Who cross-checks the trucking invoice against the booking?
... ... ...
One more time. Who cross-checks the trucking invoice against the booking?
... ... ...

The expression is: My understanding is that ... Please correct me if I'm wrong. It is a polite way to check a fact. For example, my understanding is that our team books the trucks directly. Please correct me if I'm wrong. Now say it with me.
... ... ...
My understanding is that our team books the trucks directly. Please correct me if I'm wrong.
... ... ...
One more time. My understanding is that our team books the trucks directly. Please correct me if I'm wrong.
... ... ...

The expression is: Depending on ..., we will decide whether to ... It means our decision waits for something. For example, depending on your reply, we will decide whether to buy a new PC. Now say it with me.
... ... ...
Depending on your reply, we will decide whether to buy a new PC.
... ... ...
One more time. Depending on your reply, we will decide whether to buy a new PC.
... ... ...

The expression is: upfront. It means paid first, before something happens. For example, by law, the company should pay the medical costs upfront. You used this idea yesterday in the report to the head office. Now say it with me.
... ... ...
By law, the company should pay the medical costs upfront.
... ... ...
One more time. By law, the company should pay the medical costs upfront.
... ... ...

The expression is: To meet ...'s deadline of ..., please ... by ... It is a clear way to give a deadline. For example, to meet the head office's deadline of November twentieth, please send me your numbers by noon today. Now say it with me.
... ... ...
To meet the head office's deadline of November twentieth, please send me your numbers by noon today.
... ... ...
One more time. To meet the head office's deadline of November twentieth, please send me your numbers by noon today.
... ... ...

The expression is: We were not aware that ... until ... It means we did not know something before a certain time. For example, we were not aware that the samples were declared under our name until the tax office told us. Now say it with me.
... ... ...
We were not aware that the samples were declared under our name until the tax office told us.
... ... ...
One more time. We were not aware that the samples were declared under our name until the tax office told us.
... ... ...

The expression is: Please confirm with ... whether ... It is a request to check something with another person. For example, please confirm with the broker whether they received the revised file. Now say it with me.
... ... ...
Please confirm with the broker whether they received the revised file.
... ... ...
One more time. Please confirm with the broker whether they received the revised file.
... ... ...

The expression is: Please ..., so that we can ... It gives a request and the reason together. For example, please get one more quotation, so that we can compare three suppliers. The compliance officer did exactly this yesterday with the electrical inspection. Now say it with me.
... ... ...
Please get one more quotation, so that we can compare three suppliers.
... ... ...
One more time. Please get one more quotation, so that we can compare three suppliers.
... ... ...

The expression is: approximate. It means close to the real number, but not exact. For example, the roll count can be approximate, but the yards must be correct. In a forecast, many numbers are approximate. But the tax price must be correct. Now say it with me.
... ... ...
The forecast can be approximate, but the tax price must be correct.
... ... ...
One more time. The forecast can be approximate, but the tax price must be correct.
... ... ...

The expression is: The main reason ... is that ... It explains the biggest cause. For example, the main reason the November loss is bigger is that the shipping plan changed. Now say it with me.
... ... ...
The main reason the November loss is bigger is that the shipping plan changed.
... ... ...
One more time. The main reason the November loss is bigger is that the shipping plan changed.
... ... ...
Part seven. Role-play.
Today you will show my director the first draft of the forecast. Let's practice. Anthony speaks first.
Anthony: Director, do you have five minutes? I would like to show you the first draft of the forecast.
Director: Sure. Is it until January?
Anthony: No, the head office changed it yesterday. Now it is until February. They also confirmed that every factory will fill at least a minimum share of its lines until February.
Director: Okay. What about the tax price for November?

Anthony: the chief accountant sent a new plan yesterday, because the shipping plan changed on November fourteenth. The November quantity is much bigger now. But one figure for the main buyer looks wrong, so I asked her to check it.
Director: Good. Don't approve it until the numbers match.
Anthony: Yes. Depending on her answer, I will update the forecast this afternoon.
Director: When is the deadline?
Anthony: Tomorrow, Friday. To meet the deadline, could you review the final version by tomorrow morning?
Director: Fine. Send it to me tonight.
Anthony: Thank you. I will send it before I leave today.
Now let's repeat two key sentences.

The first sentence. Depending on her answer, I will update the forecast this afternoon.
... ... ...
One more time. Depending on her answer, I will update the forecast this afternoon.
... ... ...

The second sentence. To meet the deadline, could you review the final version by tomorrow morning?
... ... ...
One more time. To meet the deadline, could you review the final version by tomorrow morning?
... ... ...
Part eight. Closing.
Let's say today's goal in one sentence. Today, I will check the chief accountant's tax price plan, finish the forecast until February, and show it to my director before I leave.

Also remember three small things. Get the full declaration check from the export team. Get the Manage versus Tax file from the cost accountant. And get the fire system quote from the compliance officer.
You did a lot yesterday. Today is about numbers, so go slowly and check twice. Have a good Thursday, Anthony. See you tomorrow.
